Subject: Annual evaluation logistics, scheduling, and appeals process

Hi team —

We need to finalize logistics for the 2026 annual evaluation window. I put together a working timeline and an initial appeals policy draft (attached). High-level asks below; please do quick redlines or call out major concerns by EOD Wed 14 Oct so we can lock communications and scheduling.

Proposed timeline (attached workbook):
- Oct 20–Nov 3: Manager calibration and review window (managers complete ratings + writeups)
- Nov 4–Nov 10: Calibration syncs and compensation recommendations sign-off
- Nov 11–Nov 17: Employee communication + 1:1s for feedback delivery
- Nov 18–Nov 25: Appeals/clarification window (employees submit appeal forms)

Key open areas:
- Appeals scope: who can appeal (rating vs. process), suggested window length (I defaulted to 7 business days)
- Sensitive roles: proposed "quiet-handback" path for ICs with export/regulatory constraints — managers to route through HR lead (Neha) vs. public comms
- Manager training: 60–75 min live session + short FAQ doc; propose Oct 25 (two time options)

Attachments: 2026_schedule_draft.xlsx, appeals-policy-draft.pdf

Please reply inline. If you want a quick sync instead of long email threads, I can book 20–30 minutes.

Thanks,
Chloe
Chloe Martin | Head of People Ops, Redwood Inference

Chloe —

Thanks for the clear plan. A couple quick notes inline:

- Appeals window: 7 business days sounds reasonable, but we should allow managers to request an extension in exceptional cases (e.g., long-term leaves) — propose language to allow HR approval for +3 days.
- Manager training: please include a short role-play slide for delivery of difficult feedback.
- Communications: can we add a FAQ bullet set specifically for international hires (timezone and local leave considerations)?

I reviewed the appeals draft at a high level — will add a few copy edits directly to the PDF.

Laura

Thanks — a few legal flags from my side (added as comments in the attached PDF):
- Appeals wording needs clearer confidentiality guarantees and a named owner for each appeal (can't leave routing ambiguous).
- For the quiet-handback path: we must document an audit trail (timestamped handoffs) and retention policy for any privileged notes.
- Consider allowing anonymous process feedback (not appeals) via a short form routed to People Ops to collect themes.

I attached redlined-appeals-feedback.pdf with suggested language and a short appendix. Happy to sync with Neha and legal counsel to finalize.

Hi Chloe + team —

Appreciate the draft. A few practical recommendations from our experience working with similar hypergrowth orgs:

1) Appeals form: keep it short (max 300 words) and require a single manager-specified rubric item to appeal (reduces scope creep).
2) Timeline: 7 business days is fine; recommend a separate 3-day "triage" window where HR confirms receipt and owner assignment. That prevents appeals from languishing.
3) Communication: provide a templated manager script for points where managers must defer to HR (e.g., compensation disputes) — include exact phrasing.

Attached is a sample appeals template (we also posted a copy to the Drive link you shared). I can draft manager-script examples if you want; happy to join the Oct 25 manager training.

Best,
Elena Morales
Senior Consultant, PeopleAdvisors

- Quiet-handback path: implement audit-trail requirement; Markus to own retention language.
